title: JSON schema for the i2 Connect server configuration file

logSettings.description: Defines how and where the server sends log messages.

serverPort.description: The port number for connectors to use. Can be overridden using the environment variable SERVER_PORT.

connectorId.description: The identifier of the connector. Can be overridden using the environment variable CONNECTOR_ID.

ssl.description: Settings for SSL connections to the server.

enabled.description: Determines whether SSL is enabled. Can be overridden using the environment variable SSL_ENABLED.

serverPort.description: The port number for SSL connections. Can be overridden using the environment variable SSL_SERVER_PORT.

certificateFile.description: The path to the .pem file for the certificate. Can be overridden using the environment variable SSL_CERTIFICATE or SSL_CERTIFICATE_FILE.

privateKeyFile.description: The path to the .pem file for the private key. Can be overridden using the environment variable SSL_PRIVATE_KEY or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE. An optional passphrase associated with this private key can be supplied in the environment variable SSL_PASSPHRASE.

caCertificateFile.description: The path to the trusted CA certificate. Can be overridden using the environment variable SSL_CA_CERTIFICATE or SSL_CA_CERTIFICATE_FILE.

gatewayCN.description: The gateway common name, which can be a string or an array of strings. Can be overridden using the environment variable SSL_GATEWAY_CN.

enabled.description: Determines whether file logging is enabled. Can be overridden using the environment variable LOG_FILE_LOGGING_ENABLED.

dir.description: The directory to log to. Can be overridden using the environment variable LOG_FILE_LOGGING_DIR.

level.description: The minimum message level to log. Messages at lower levels are ignored. Can be overridden using the environment variable LOG_LEVEL.

The minimum message level to log. Messages at lower levels are ignored. Can be overridden using the environment variable LOG_X_LEVEL, where X is the identifier of the additional logger in uppercase letters.

requestOrigin.description: Settings for determining the request origin URL for file and resource references.

frontEndUri.description: The complete front-end URI (protocol, host, port and path as mapped by any proxy) to use for file and resource references. When specified, this overrides all header-based detection and frontEndUriPath is ignored. Use this when header based detection is not sufficient for your case. Example: 'https://example.eia:9443/connectors/my-connector/api' where 'connectors/my-connector/api' is the proxy re-mapped path. Can be overridden using the environment variable FRONT_END_URI.

frontEndUriPath.description: The path component to append to the detected protocol and host (from requested headers) for file and resource references. Only used when frontEndUri is not set. Useful if proxies are re-mapping the URI with additional paths, but the protocol, host and port will be detected from headers. Example: '/connectors/my-connector/api' to produce 'https://example.eia:9443/connectors/my-connector/api'. Can be overridden using the environment variable FRONT_END_URI_PATH.

jwtCertificateFile.description: The path to the trusted JWT certificate file for verifying JWT tokens. Can be overridden using the environment variable JWT_CERTIFICATE_FILE or JWT_CERTIFICATE_FILE_PATH.
